title: Turn up the spillover

predict.q: The external benefit per unit rises from 0 to 8. What happens?

options.s: Buyers notice the extra benefit, so the market quantity rises to the optimum.
options.fb: Buyers respond only to their own benefit (MPB), which has not moved, so Q1 stays put.

options.s: The optimum falls, because the benefit is now spread over more people.
options.fb: A bigger external benefit raises MSB, so the optimum rises, not falls.

options.s: The market quantity stays the same, the optimum rises and the welfare loss grows.
options.fb: Q1 stays at 120; Q* rises from 120 to 160; the welfare loss grows from 0 to 160.

options.s: Nothing changes, because external benefits are not part of any curve.
options.fb: External benefits are shown by the gap between MPB and MSB; MSB moves up.

task: Move the external benefit slider and watch MSB, Q* and the shaded triangle.

target.do: Move the slider from 0 to 8, then press Check.

takeaway: The market ignores external benefits, so the bigger they are, the further Q1 falls short of Q*.
